newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuadoran oil company ready to work with state.
newsitem.headline: Ecuadoran oil company ready to work with state.

text.p: Ecuadoran oil company Tripetrol is prepared to renegotiate its contract with the government to explore and operate the coastal Santa Elena field, the private company said Monday.
Tripetrol President Jose Pesafiel said in a press release it is ready to change its contract in favor of one with mixed state and private participation in the operation of the field.

"According to the current contract, the participation of the state would only start when the company had recuperated all its investment, which could delay it for many years," said Pesafiel. Tripetrol, owned by Ecuadoran interests, said it has invested $60 million so far in the field.
"Tripetrol expects that the stability and conditions of the new contract will help the total development of the Pacoa oil field with the necessary investments," the statement said.

Tripetrol started operating an onshore oil field together with state oil company Petroecuador at the beginning of this year. Tripetrol has operated and explored the Santa Elena sector since 1989, when it took over Belco's operations.
The Ecuadoran oil firm's statement came just days after the government suspended the operations of U.S. oil company Maxus for not wanting to mix its operations with Petroecuador.
